summary_en.core_problem: The paper diagnoses cases where pairwise alignment appears valid for model merging but fails to yield globally consistent multi-model alignment, with abstention when certification fails.
summary_en.importance: The contribution is a theoretical diagnostic framework for model merging. It is indirectly relevant to merging fine-tuned checkpoints, adapters, or model soups, but it is not central to LLM pretraining.
summary_en.technical_approach: Model merging is formulated as a finite descent problem: checkpoints are local objects, alignment maps are transitions, and cycle products are residuals. TwistedMerge separates fixed-chart averaging, synchronization-removable gauge inconsistency, certified central obstruction, and nonabelian holonomy, promoting residuals only after inverse-consistency, coefficient-identification, centrality, and closure tests.
summary_en.experiments: The abstract reports constant-edge no-go, error-control theorems for frozen-complex three-way and predeclared families, and a refinement test for comparison-complex sensitivity. A planted neural alignment defect is removed by cycle-consistent synchronization, but no LLM-scale benchmark evidence is described.

recommendation.zh: 数学味很重，实际信号只在“pairwise merge 不保证全局一致”这点；做 checkpoint 合并时可查，不建议投入长读。
recommendation.en: The useful signal is the warning that pairwise mergeability does not imply global consistency; keep it as a reference for checkpoint merging, not a long read.

paper.title: ISO: An RLVR-Native Optimization Stack
paper.abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) is rapidly advancing the reasoning capabilities of language models, yet the optimization layer that converts reward feedback into weight-space updates remains poorly understood. Building on our prior analysis (Zhu et al., 2025), we study this missing layer through the singular structure of model weights and identify spectral inheritance: RLVR can reuse the base model's weight spectra while acquiring new behavior through changes in the associa

summary.core_problem: RLVR 已经成为提升大模型推理能力的主要 post-training 手段，但其优化层仍然直接沿用预训练阶段的优化器与参数化方式（AdamW、Muon 等），没有回答一个基本问题：RLVR 在权重空间里到底改动了什么、复用了什么？论文要找的是一个适合 RLVR 的参数化坐标系，让优化动作和“继承 base model 能力、增量学习推理行为”这一结构相匹配。
summary.importance: 对 pretrain ↔ posttrain 接口的理解有实质性推进。Spectral inheritance 把之前零散观察到的 RL 更新稀疏、跨 run 重叠、与 SFT 的 Euclidean 轨迹不同等现象，统一到了 SVD 坐标系下的一个可操作结论：奇异值谱被复用，输入/输出奇异方向（singular frames）被改写。这个结论直接影响优化器设计、checkpoint 合并、持续学习与多阶段 RL 的 recipe，和 Apollo、Muon 这类 optimizer 工作处在同一问题层，但切入角度是“RLVR 改变了什么结构”，而不是“在欧氏空间里怎么更好地更新”。
summary.technical_approach: 以每个权重矩阵的 SVD 分解 W = U Σ V^⊤ 为基本坐标系：Σ 是奇异值谱，U / V 分别是输出/输入奇异 frame。核心观察是：自由训练的 RLVR checkpoint 与 base 模型近等谱（near-isospectral），且这种谱接近不是单纯高维几何的必然结果；进一步做了三组干预实验验证功能必要性：(1) 将 RL checkpoint 的 Σ 恢复为 base 的 Σ，保留学到的 U、V，绝大部分 RL 收益仍然保留；(2) 训练时固定 Σ、只更新 U 和 V，仍然能强化学到 RLVR 能力；(3) 反过来固定 U、V、只更新 Σ，几乎学不到东西。由此提出 spectral inheritance：base 的谱可以被继承，行为改变主要发生在两个 frame 上。随后验证了两个 frame 都必须可塑，只在输入/输出 span 内 remix、或只放开单侧 frame 都无法解释完整的 checkpoint 变化。基于此提出 ISO（Isospectral Optimization）栈，包含两块：ISO-Merger（离线）：共享同一 base 的多个 domain specialist，不通过额外蒸馏或梯度更新，直接在固定 base 谱的前提下把各专家的 frame 变化合并成一个单一 checkpoint，能恢复互补能力；ISO-Optimizer（在线）：在 RLVR 训练过程中把参数化约束在 base 谱对应的固定谱流形上，允许 frame 自由更新，可以搭配 AdamW/Muon 等现有 base optimizer 使用。
summary.experiments: 实验跨多个 RLVR stage 和目标函数展开（文中提到承接自 zhu2025path 的分析，并覆盖类似 DAPO / Reinforce++ 等不同 RL 目标阶段），关键结果包括：自由 RLVR 训练中 Σ 的漂移远小于 frame 变化，且谱恢复实验证明保留 frame 就能保留绝大多数收益；固定谱训练（仅更新 U、V）达到与自由训练接近的 RL 收益，而只更新 Σ 的对照组只有有限提升；ISO-Merger 在无数据、无额外 rollout、无蒸馏条件下，对多个共享 base 的 specialist 做 checkpoint 合并，在各项聚合指标上优于所对比的 data-free 合并方法；ISO-Optimizer 配合 AdamW / Muon 可稳定训练并保持 RLVR 收益。消融系统地比较了单 frame 可塑、span-restricted remix、全自由更新等多种参数化，确认“两个 frame 都可动、谱可固定”是必要且充分的结构选择。
summary.reading_guide: 精读，建议 1–1.5 小时。重点章节按顺序看：(1) Introduction 到 spectral inheritance 定义部分——这里建立了与 pretrain/SFT 的结构性差异，是整篇论文的 conceptual core；(2) 近等谱观测与高维校准那一节——注意区分“几何上自然接近”和“功能上可复用”这两件事，校准部分很关键，避免误读为“高维里啥都不动”；(3) 谱恢复 / 固定谱训练 / 仅谱更新三个对照实验（核心图和表）——这是支持 inheritance 的硬证据；(4) two-frame adaptability 的消融，理解为什么单侧或 span-restricted 不够；(5) ISO-Merger 和 ISO-Optimizer 两节，看具体参数化如何落地，特别是 frame 优化是否需要额外正则化、与 KKT/黎曼优化/正交约束的关系。值得深挖的点：这套观察是否能外推到 SFT/持续预训练、MoE 专家权重、不同层（attention vs MLP）是否表现一致；以及 frame 更新和已有 optimizer（Muon 的正交更新、Apollo 的子空间投影）之间的关联。
summary.authors_note: 作者承接 zhu2025path 系列工作，聚焦 RLVR 优化与权重空间几何；机构信息文中未明确给出。

summary_en.core_problem: RLVR has become a primary axis for improving LLM reasoning, yet the optimization layer that turns sparse outcome rewards into weight updates is largely inherited from pretraining (AdamW, Muon, etc.). The question is what RLVR actually changes in weight space versus what it reuses from the base model, and whether an RLVR-native parameterization exists that matches this structure.
summary_en.importance: Substantial contribution to understanding the pretrain–posttrain interface. Spectral inheritance unifies previously scattered observations—sparse but consistent Euclidean updates across runs, marked differences from SFT trajectories, limited overall motion—into an operable SVD-coordinate story: base singular-value spectra are largely reused, while behavior change is carried by the input and output singular frames. This has direct implications for optimizer design, checkpoint merging, continual post-training, and multi-stage RL recipes. It sits at the same level as optimizer work like Muon and Apollo, but attacks the problem by identifying what structure RLVR should preserve rather than by improving Euclidean updates.
summary_en.technical_approach: Each weight matrix is analyzed in its SVD basis W = U Σ V^⊤, with Σ the singular-value spectrum and (U, V) the output/input singular frames. The central empirical observation is that freely trained RLVR checkpoints stay near-isospectral to their base, and this proximity is not merely a high-dimensional artifact. Three interventions test functional necessity: (1) restoring base Σ while keeping learned U, V in RL checkpoints preserves most acquired gains; (2) training with Σ fixed throughout RL while updating only U and V still achieves strong RL learning; (3) the reverse—freezing frames and updating only Σ—yields only marginal improvement. This leads to spectral inheritance: the base spectrum can be reused, with new behavior carried by both frames. Follow-up ablations show both frames must remain adaptable; remixing only within input/output spans or holding one frame fixed leaves substantially more of the endpoint change unexplained. ISO (Isospectral Optimization) operationalizes this in two complementary forms. ISO-Merger (offline) consolidates multiple specialists trained from a shared base by reusing the shared base spectra and directly combining expert frame changes into a single fixed-spectrum checkpoint, without extra data, rollouts, or distillation. ISO-Optimizer (online) constrains training to the fixed-spectrum manifold of the base weights while allowing both frames to adapt, and can be wrapped around base optimizers such as AdamW or Muon.
summary_en.experiments: Experiments span multiple RLVR stages and objectives (building on zhu2025path and covering objectives in the family of DAPO, Reinforce++, etc.). Key findings include: free RLVR produces much smaller drift in Σ than in U/V; spectrum-restoration and fixed-spectrum training retain most gains, while spectrum-only training does not; ISO-Merger consolidates complementary specialists better than compared data-free merging baselines, with no post-merge data or gradient updates; ISO-Optimizer trains stably on top of AdamW/Muon while preserving RLVR performance. Systematic ablations compare single-frame adaptability, span-restricted remixing, and free updates, establishing that fixing the spectrum while keeping both frames adaptable is the minimal sufficient structural choice among the tested alternatives.
summary_en.reading_guide: Read carefully, about 1–1.5 hours. Recommended order: (1) Introduction through the definition of spectral inheritance—this is the conceptual core and situates RLVR against pretraining and SFT; (2) the near-isospectrality observation together with the high-dimensional calibration—important for distinguishing geometric proximity from functional reusability; (3) the three key interventions (spectrum restoration, fixed-spectrum training, spectrum-only training) — the strongest evidence for inheritance; (4) ablations on two-frame adaptability, to see why one-sided or span-restricted variants are insufficient; (5) ISO-Merger and ISO-Optimizer sections for how the parameterization is implemented in practice, especially how frame updates are regularized and how the scheme relates to Riemannian/orthogonal constraints. Points worth digging into: whether the same pattern holds for SFT and continual pretraining, whether attention and MLP weights behave differently, how frame-level updates relate to Muon’s orthogonal updates and Apollo’s subspace projections, and whether the story extends to MoE experts.
summary_en.authors_note: Follow-up work to the zhu2025path line on RL optimization and weight-space geometry; explicit institutional affiliations not stated in the provided text.

recommendation.zh: 把 RL 后权重的 SVD 结构讲清楚了，ISO-Merger 是无蒸馏合并 specialist 的实用新范式，应在内部 RL 流水线复现。
recommendation.en: Cleanly characterizes post-RL weight structure via SVD; ISO-Merger is a practical new paradigm for merging specialists without distillation—worth reproducing in internal RL pipelines.

paper.title: When Model Merging Rivals Joint Multi-Task Reinforcement Learning: A Task-Vector Geometry Analysis
paper.abstract: Model merging is promoted as a substitute for joint multi-task training, yet in the reinforcement-learning setting this substitution is essentially never tested against the baseline it claims to replace: methods merge independently released agents precisely because a joint model is unavailable. We build the missing comparison. Training difficulty-1 and difficulty-2 Qwen3-8B specialists on the AppWorld agent benchmark with LOOP, we merge them (TIES, RAM+) and pit the result against a jointly trai

summary.core_problem: 这篇论文要解决的问题很明确：在强化学习训练的 agent 场景里，model merging 常被当作 joint multi-task RL 的替代方案，但几乎没人把它和真正可得的 joint training baseline 正面比较。作者在一个可控设定里补上了这个缺口：当多任务数据其实可以合并训练时，合并两个 RL specialist 得到的 merged model，和直接在任务并集上做 joint RL，到底谁更好；如果两者差不多，原因是什么。论文进一步把问题落到 task-vector geometry 上，试图用参数空间中的方向关系解释“为什么 merge 方法差别不大”。
summary.importance: 它和基座预训练的直接距离较远，因为主体是 post-training / RL agent，而不是 pretrain。但有两点仍有启发。第一，它提供了一个很干净的负结果：在 LoRA RL specialist 的这个 regime 里，merge 与 joint RL 在主指标上打平，说明很多关于 merge rule 设计的收益，可能先被任务噪声和向量几何结构淹没。第二，它把 task vector 的“支持重叠”和“方向近正交”区分开来，这对理解参数高维空间中的任务干扰、adapter 叠加、continual finetuning 乃至多域 mid-training 都有参考价值。贡献类型更像是受控比较和诊断分析，而不是提出新方法。
summary.technical_approach:
方法上，作者构造了一个尽量公平的比较框架。所有模型都从同一个 Qwen3-8B base 出发，用相同 LoRA 配置、相同 RL recipe、相同 benchmark。训练三个核心对象：difficulty-1 specialist、difficulty-2 specialist，以及在两类任务并集上训练的 joint model。然后把两个 specialist 的 task vector 做 merge，主要测试 TIES 和 RAM+ 这类方法。

论文的技术重点不在 merge 算法本身，而在几何诊断。因为所有 specialist 都用相同 LoRA target modules，所以 task vectors 的 support 是天然重合的；这排除了“因为更新位置不同所以不冲突”的简单解释。作者转而测量方向几何，尤其是 task vector cosine similarity，并做了 floor/ceiling calibration，避免把“低秩 LoRA 导致余弦小”误判为真正的任务解耦。结果显示两个 specialist 的 task vectors 虽然 support overlap 很大，但方向接近正交，cosine 只有 0.06–0.10。作者据此解释：既然共享子空间中的冲突分量本来就很小，那么 TIES 这类按符号或支持做 disentangle 的 merge 规则，自然没有太大发挥空间。

RL 训练方面，虽然名义上使用 LOOP，实际由于算力限制采用的是 on-policy、单次更新、无 rollout reuse 的配置，因此等价于 RLOO/REINFORCE with leave-one-out baseline。这个细节很重要，因为它说明实验中的 specialist 不是强 PPO-style off-policy RL 产物，而是较轻量的 on-policy policy gradient 结果。也就是说，结论适用的 regime 更接近“LoRA + 轻量 RL 调整”的 agent specialization，而不是大规模深度 RL。
summary.experiments:
核心实验结论很集中。作者在 AppWorld 上训练两个 specialist 和一个 joint model，并在 168 个 held-out test_normal 任务上比较 task-goal completion。结果是：所有 merge 变体与 joint RL 在 TGC 上统计上不可区分，真正显著的提升只来自“做了 RL”相对于 base model，而不是“用哪种多任务整合方式”。这意味着在 8B、约 10 次 RL iterations、任务难度差距只有 1–2 档的设定下，merge 与 joint 的差异落在噪声墙之下。

几何分析给出更细的解释：specialist task vectors 的 cosine 约为 0.06–0.10，接近正交；而且这种小的共享分量是在训练过程中逐步形成的，不是初始化或 LoRA 低秩约束的假象。作者还强调 support overlap 很大，因此“近正交”不是因为更新模块不同。

论文还报告了一个值得谨慎看待的现象：如果换成连续 partial-credit metric，merged models 会低于未合并模型，似乎显示 merge 有损。但作者进一步说明，这个差异并不代表 joint/merge 产生了新的跨任务能力，也不能通过 trajectory-aware checkpoint selection 弥补；而且该指标与 TGC 的排序会反转，说明结论对 metric 很敏感。这个部分的价值在于提醒读者：agent RL 里评测指标的分辨率和噪声结构，会直接决定你能否看见 merge/joint 的真实差异。
summary.reading_guide: 泛读建议是先抓三处。第一，看实验设定部分，确认比较是否公平：同一 base、同一 LoRA、同一 RL recipe、同一数据预算。第二，看主结果表和统计检验，重点不是均值谁高一点，而是作者如何证明“不可区分”。第三，看 task-vector geometry 分析，尤其是 cosine 的定义、校准方法、以及 support overlap 与 direction orthogonality 的区分。若时间有限，可以略过 merge 方法细节推导，因为论文的主要信息不是提出新 merge rule，而是说明在这个 regime 下 rule 之间没有可见差异。预计 25–35 分钟能读完主线；若想把它和参数高维干扰问题联系起来，再细看 §5.2、§5.3 和关于 checkpoint selection 无效的分析。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper addresses a missing baseline question in RL model merging: when joint multi-task RL is actually feasible, does merging independently trained RL specialists match a jointly trained model, and if so, why? Most prior merging work in agent settings studies the case where a joint model is unavailable, so the claimed substitute is rarely compared against the thing it is supposed to replace. The authors build a controlled comparison and then use task-vector geometry to explain the outcome.
summary_en.importance: This is not a pretraining paper, but it is still relevant at the interface between parameter-space adaptation, continual specialization, and post-training. Its main value is a careful null result. In this LoRA-based RL regime, merging matches joint multi-task RL on the primary metric, and different merge rules are statistically indistinguishable. That is useful because it suggests that, before attributing gains to sophisticated merge heuristics, one should check whether the task vectors are already geometrically non-interfering. The paper also makes a useful distinction between support overlap and directional overlap, which matters for thinking about adapter composition, multi-domain tuning, and interference analysis more broadly.
summary_en.technical_approach:
The setup is designed to be as controlled as possible. All models start from the same Qwen3-8B base, use the same LoRA configuration, the same RL recipe, and the same benchmark. The authors train two specialists on AppWorld subsets split by difficulty level, plus a joint model trained on the union of those tasks. They then merge the two specialists using standard methods such as TIES and RAM+.

The technical center of the paper is not a new merge rule but a geometric diagnosis of why merge method barely matters here. Because all specialists adapt the same LoRA target modules, their task vectors have overlapping support by construction. This rules out the trivial explanation that they simply modify disjoint parameters. The authors therefore measure directional geometry, especially cosine similarity between task vectors, and calibrate the measurement with floor and ceiling references so that small cosine values cannot be dismissed as a low-rank LoRA artifact. The key finding is that the specialists’ task vectors are nearly orthogonal, with cosine around 0.06–0.10, despite large support overlap. If the conflicting shared component is already tiny, then support-aware or sign-aware merge rules have little left to disentangle.

A notable implementation detail is that, although the paper frames training in terms of LOOP, the actual compute-constrained regime is on-policy with one update per rollout batch and no rollout reuse. In effect, this reduces to RLOO / REINFORCE with a leave-one-out baseline rather than a stronger PPO-style off-policy variant. That matters for interpreting the scope of the result: it is about LoRA specialists produced by relatively lightweight RL, not deeply optimized large-scale RL agents.
summary_en.experiments:
The main empirical result is simple. On AppWorld, the authors compare two specialists, their merges, and a joint model on 168 held-out test_normal tasks using task-goal completion. All merge variants and the joint model are statistically indistinguishable on TGC. The only clear gain is RL over the base model. In other words, at 8B scale, with roughly 10 RL iterations and only a 1–2 difficulty margin between task groups, the merge-vs-joint differences sit below the noise floor.

The geometry analysis provides the explanation. The specialists’ task vectors have cosine similarity around 0.06–0.10, i.e. close to orthogonal, and the paper argues that this is not an artifact of low-rank LoRA. At the same time, support overlap is large because the same modules are adapted. So the vectors overlap in where they act, but not much in the directions they push.

The paper also reports a metric-sensitivity result. Under a continuous partial-credit metric, merged models look worse than the unmerged ones. The authors caution against over-interpreting this: the ranking can reverse relative to TGC, the effect does not indicate emergent cross-task capability, and trajectory-aware checkpoint selection does not recover the gap. This is a useful reminder that in agent RL, the apparent difference between merge and joint training can depend heavily on the evaluation metric’s resolution and noise properties.
summary_en.reading_guide: Skim the paper with three focal points. First, verify the fairness of the setup: same base model, same LoRA targets, same RL recipe, same data budget. Second, read the main results table and the statistical testing carefully; the point is not tiny mean differences but the claim of indistinguishability. Third, spend time on the task-vector geometry section, especially how cosine is measured, how the floor/ceiling calibration is done, and why support overlap does not imply directional interference. You can safely skim the merge-rule details unless you specifically care about TIES or RAM+, because the paper’s main contribution is the controlled comparison and the diagnosis, not a new algorithm. About 25–35 minutes should be enough for the main line.

recommendation.zh: 读 task-vector 几何和 joint RL 对照即可；若 setup 干净，内部多任务 RL 合并实验应复现这个基线。
recommendation.en: Read the task-vector geometry and joint-RL comparison; if the setup is clean, this baseline should be replicated in internal multitask RL merging tests.

paper.title: Leveraging Instruction Tuning and Merging for Reasoning Model Adaptation
paper.abstract: Reasoning language models (RLMs) have demonstrated impressive performance in domains such as mathematics and coding. These domains permit reliable verification of model outputs, which is important for enabling the reinforcement learning that drives RLM performance gains. However, training RLMs on domains that lack reliable verifiers remains challenging. Meanwhile, for both verifiable and unverifiable domains, large amounts of unused supervised fine-tuning data with human-written solutions exist.

summary.core_problem: 推理模型在缺乏可靠验证器的领域难以继续提升，同时大量无推理轨迹的人工解答SFT数据未被有效利用。
summary.importance: 方法创新：提出指令微调和模型合并结合的两阶段方案，低成本复用无推理轨迹的监督数据增强推理模型。
summary.technical_approach: 先对原始推理模型做不含思维链的经典指令微调，再将微调后模型与原推理模型做参数合并，在保留推理行为的同时吸收监督数据的知识。
summary.experiments: 覆盖可验证（数学、代码）与难验证领域，对比原推理模型基线，合并后模型在两类场景均取得稳定性能提升。
summary.authors_note: Martin Vechev 团队（ETH Zurich Secure, Reliable, and Intelligent Systems Lab），长期从事程序合成、LLM推理与安全研究。

summary_en.core_problem: Reasoning LLMs struggle to improve in domains without reliable verifiers, while large volumes of SFT data with human-written solutions but no reasoning traces remain unused.
summary_en.importance: Methodological contribution: a low-cost two-stage recipe that repurposes trace-free supervised data to further boost reasoning models.
summary_en.technical_approach: First perform standard instruction tuning (without CoT traces) on the base reasoning model, then merge the instruction-tuned checkpoint back with the original reasoning model to recover reasoning behavior while absorbing new knowledge.
summary_en.experiments: Evaluated across verifiable (math, coding) and hard-to-verify domains; the merged model consistently outperforms the original reasoning model baseline on both settings.
summary_en.authors_note: Martin Vechev's group at ETH Zurich's SRI Lab, known for work on program synthesis, LLM reasoning, and trustworthy ML.

recommendation.zh: 作为低成本后训练技巧备查，合并策略细节可参考，但对预训练本身无直接方法论推进。
recommendation.en: Useful as a low-cost post-training trick to reference; no direct methodological advance for pretraining itself.

paper.title: Are we Merging the Right Models? Impact of Expert Training Duration on Model Merging for LLMs
paper.abstract: Multi-task model merging combines separately trained expert models into a single model that handles all tasks without co-training. Standard practice merges experts at their optimal validation loss. We challenge this convention by systematically studying how training duration of domain experts affects the quality of the merged model. We fine-tune experts on five domains (Math, Code, Instruction Following, Multilingual, and Safety) across three model sizes (Qwen 3.5 0.8B, 2B, and 4B), saving check

summary.core_problem: 这篇工作要回答的不是“哪种 merge 方法更好”，而是一个更前置的问题：用于合并的专家模型，应该在什么训练阶段被拿来 merge。现有做法几乎默认取各自验证集最优 checkpoint，再做 averaging、task arithmetic 或 TIES 一类的权重空间合并。作者系统检验后发现，这个默认前提对 decoder-only LLM 并不稳。专家训练时长会显著改变 merged model 的质量，而且最优时长强烈依赖 merge 方法本身。更具体地说，简单平均更偏好欠训练专家；带冲突消解和稀疏化的 TIES / DARE+TIES 反而在明显过拟合之后达到最好结果。论文真正解决的是“单模型最优”和“可合并性最优”并不一致这一问题，并试图给出机制解释。
summary.importance: 对预训练/后训练接口的启发主要有两层。第一层是工程层面：如果企业或研究团队在做多域 LoRA 专家训练再 merge，早停点不该再被当成固定 recipe，而应视 merge 算法共同决定的超参。第二层是方法层面：论文把 model merging 从“静态算法比较”推进到“训练轨迹上的 mergeability 分析”，这比单纯比较 TIES、DARE、Soup 的最终分数更有信息量。它说明专家间的多样性、干扰结构和参数符号冲突，会随着训练继续发生系统变化；而 merge 方法的优劣，部分取决于它能否利用这种后期多样性并抑制干扰。量级上，这不是改写预训练范式的工作，但对小中型开源模型的多任务适配、持续增量训练、模块化后训练都有直接参考价值。
summary.technical_approach:
实验设计比较干净。作者选了 Qwen 3.5 的 0.8B、2B、4B 三个尺度，在 Math、Code、Instruction Following、Multilingual、Safety 五个域上分别做 QLoRA 专家微调。LoRA rank 为 16，底座 4-bit 量化，目标模块覆盖 attention 和 MLP projection。训练使用常数学习率 2e-4、100 step warmup、AdamW、effective batch size 8，而且故意不做学习率衰减，这样模型在验证最优点之后仍会持续更新，便于观察过拟合阶段的 merge 效应。每个专家先独立确定验证损失最优步数 T*，再保存 0.25x、0.5x、0.75x、1x、1.5x、2x、3x、5x T* 的 checkpoint。

随后作者把五个域的 LoRA adapter 在同一底座上做合并，比较五类方法：Simple Averaging、Task Arithmetic、TIES、DARE+TIES、Greedy Soup。Task Arithmetic 的缩放系数 λ 在 {0.5, 1.0, 1.5} 上网格搜索；TIES 和 DARE+TIES 的 density 设为 0.5。核心发现是 merge 方法对专家训练时长的偏好呈现稳定分层：
1. Simple Averaging 在较早 checkpoint 最好，随着专家继续训练明显恶化；
2. Task Arithmetic 和 Greedy Soup 处于中间区间，通常接近验证最优或略晚；
3. TIES 与 DARE+TIES 在过拟合区间达到峰值，往往要到 1.5x、2x 甚至更晚。

机制分析主要借了两个视角。一个是 bias-variance-covariance decomposition。作者把 merged model 的泛化误差拆成平均偏差、个体方差和专家间协方差，类比 random forest 中“深树虽然单体过拟合，但因相关性下降，集成后反而更好”的现象。这里的对应关系是：过训练专家虽然单体更差，但参数更新更分散、域特化更强，给 merge 带来更高多样性；若 merge 方法有能力处理冲突参数，这种多样性可以转化为收益。另一个是 mode connectivity / loss barrier 分析。作者检查不同训练时长下专家之间以及专家到 merged model 之间的连通性和障碍高度，说明过拟合后专家更远离彼此、线性插值障碍更高，简单平均因此更容易落到坏区域；而 TIES/DARE 通过裁剪小幅更新、解决符号冲突、保留一致方向的大幅 delta，能更好地从分散专家中抽取可兼容信号。这个解释比“过拟合有时有益”更具体，关键不在过拟合本身，而在过拟合带来的多样性是否能被 merge 机制消化。
summary.experiments:
实验覆盖 3 个模型尺度、5 个任务域、8 个训练时长、5 种 merge 方法，主结果看四个 accuracy 类任务的平均分，Safety 单独看 HarmBench 上 refuse-to-answer。全文给出的核心结论是趋势非常稳定，而不是只在单一模型上偶然成立。

从结果形态看，Figure 1 是最关键的：Simple Averaging 随训练时长增加持续下滑，说明它对后期专家分化极其敏感；TIES 和 DARE+TIES 则在 1x T* 之后继续上升，并在明显过拟合区间达到最好；Task Arithmetic 与 Greedy Soup 的峰值更靠近中间。作者强调这种模式在 0.8B、2B、4B 上都能观察到，只是峰值位置和幅度会随尺度变化。Safety 结果也不是例外：拒答率随 merge 方法和训练时长同样呈现方法依赖的最优点，而不是统一地“越早越好”或“越晚越好”。

消融和分析部分的价值在于把现象拆开。一个重要观察是，随着训练超过 T*，单个专家验证性能下降，但专家之间的差异性上升。若 merge 方法没有冲突处理，这种差异性直接变成 destructive interference；若 merge 方法能做稀疏化和符号对齐，差异性的一部分会转成互补性。作者还比较了不同方法在不同时长下的 merged-vs-best-expert 差距，说明“拿最优单专家 checkpoint merge”并不等于“得到最优 merged model”。摘要里没有给出大量具体数值，全文重点也更偏趋势和机制，而不是追求某个单点提升数字。阅读时应把注意力放在曲线形状、峰值位置和分析图，而不是只找一个平均提升百分点。
summary.reading_guide:
建议先看 Introduction 最后两段和 Figure 1，先建立一个清晰预期：这篇文章不是在发明新 merge 算法，而是在改写 merge 实验的默认 protocol。然后看 Experimental Setup，重点确认三件事：为什么用常数学习率、为什么用相对时长 T* 而不是绝对 step、为什么选五个域和五种 merge 方法。接着精读 Results 中按方法分组的主曲线，尤其比较 averaging 与 TIES/DARE 的峰值位置差异。

如果时间有限，最值得细看的部分是 bias-variance-covariance decomposition 和 mode connectivity 分析。前者给出“过训练专家为何可能更适合被 merge”的统计解释；后者解释“为什么简单平均会坏，而稀疏化方法还能受益”。这两部分决定了论文是否只是经验观察，还是对 mergeability 有更一般的理解。附录里完整分域结果也值得扫一遍，用来判断结论是否被某一域主导。预计泛读 25-35 分钟，若要真正吸收其方法论价值，连同附录和图表一起读大约 1 小时。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper asks a more fundamental question than “which merging method works best”: at what training stage should expert models be merged? Standard practice in model merging takes each expert at its own validation-optimal checkpoint and treats that as the natural input to merging. This work shows that, for decoder-only LLM experts, that assumption is unreliable. The best checkpoint for an individual expert is often not the best checkpoint for the merged model, and the optimal training duration depends strongly on the merging algorithm. Simple averaging prefers undertrained experts, while sparsification-based methods such as TIES and DARE+TIES often peak well after the experts have passed their own validation optimum.
summary_en.importance: Its main value is methodological rather than benchmark-driven. For practical LLM adaptation pipelines—especially multi-domain LoRA training followed by weight-space merging—the paper argues that early stopping should not be treated as a fixed recipe independent of the merge method. More broadly, it shifts the discussion from static comparisons of merge algorithms to a trajectory-level view of mergeability: how expert diversity, interference, and parameter conflict evolve over training, and how different merging rules exploit or fail under those dynamics. This is not a pretraining paper in the narrow sense, but it is relevant to continual adaptation, modular post-training, and the interface between optimization trajectories and parameter-space composition.
summary_en.technical_approach:
The setup is systematic and fairly controlled. The authors use Qwen 3.5 models at 0.8B, 2B, and 4B scales. For each scale, they fine-tune domain experts with QLoRA (rank 16) on top of a 4-bit quantized base model, targeting all attention and MLP projection modules. Training uses AdamW, constant learning rate 2e-4, 100-step warmup, and effective batch size 8. The constant LR is deliberate: it keeps optimization active beyond the validation optimum so that the experts can move into clearly overfitted regimes.

They train experts on five domains—Math, Code, Instruction Following, Multilingual, and Safety. For each expert, they identify its own validation-optimal step T* and then save checkpoints at 0.25x, 0.5x, 0.75x, 1.0x, 1.5x, 2.0x, 3.0x, and 5.0x T*. These checkpoints are then merged across all five domains using five methods: Simple Averaging, Task Arithmetic, TIES, DARE+TIES, and Greedy Soup.

The central empirical pattern is method-dependent and stable across scales. Simple Averaging peaks early and degrades sharply as experts continue training. Task Arithmetic and Greedy Soup prefer an intermediate regime, often around or slightly after T*. TIES and DARE+TIES peak later, often in clearly overfitted regions. The paper then explains this with two analytical lenses. First, a bias-variance-covariance decomposition: overtrained experts may generalize worse individually, but they become more diverse, and methods with interference-resolution mechanisms can convert that diversity into gains. Second, mode connectivity / loss barrier analysis: as experts train longer, they drift farther apart in weight space, making naive linear averaging more likely to land in poor regions, while sparsification and sign-resolution help preserve compatible directions and suppress destructive conflicts. The contribution is not just the empirical observation that “overfitting can help,” but a more precise claim: later checkpoints are useful when the merge rule can harvest diversity without inheriting all the interference.
summary_en.experiments:
The study spans 3 model sizes, 5 domains, 8 training durations, and 5 merging methods. The main metric aggregates the four accuracy-based domains, while Safety is evaluated separately with refuse-to-answer rate on HarmBench. The most important result is the shape of the performance curves rather than a single headline number.

Figure 1 appears to be the key result: Simple Averaging deteriorates as expert training extends beyond T*, indicating strong sensitivity to late-stage expert divergence. TIES and DARE+TIES continue improving past T* and often reach their best merged performance in overfitted regimes. Task Arithmetic and Greedy Soup sit in between. The paper states that this qualitative pattern holds across 0.8B, 2B, and 4B models, though the exact peak location and gain size vary by scale.

The analysis sections are more informative than raw averages. One recurring observation is that after T*, individual expert validation quality drops while inter-expert diversity increases. For averaging, that diversity mostly manifests as destructive interference. For TIES/DARE-style methods, part of it becomes complementary signal once small deltas are trimmed and sign conflicts are resolved. The paper also compares merged performance against the best single expert across durations, reinforcing the point that validation-optimal experts are not necessarily merge-optimal experts. The abstract and visible text do not expose many exact numeric improvements, so the paper is best read for its robust trends, peak shifts, and mechanistic analysis rather than for one isolated gain figure.
summary_en.reading_guide:
Start with the end of the introduction and the main result figure. The key framing is that the paper is not proposing a new merge algorithm; it is revising the default experimental protocol used to evaluate and deploy existing ones. Then read the setup carefully, especially the reasons for using constant LR, relative duration T* instead of absolute steps, and the chosen domain/method coverage.

The most important sections are the main duration-performance curves and the two analysis blocks: bias-variance-covariance decomposition and mode connectivity. Those sections contain the real insight. They explain why late checkpoints hurt averaging yet help sparsification-based merging, and they make the paper more than a collection of empirical curves. If time is limited, a solid skim is about 25–35 minutes. A more useful read, including appendices with per-domain results, is closer to an hour.

recommendation.zh: 模型合并的反常识发现：稀疏化方法不用卡最优checkpoint，过拟合后合并效果更好，做模型融合的重点看§4结果和Fig 4。
recommendation.en: Counterintuitive finding on LLM merging: sparsification-based methods peak past validation optimum. Focus on §4 results and Fig 4 if you work on model fusion.

paper.abstract: Continual learning commonly relies on post-hoc mechanisms such as replay, elastic regularization, or distillation. This work argues that forgetting should instead be modeled directly as interference between tasks. In the frozen-feature regime, forgetting from learning a new task is exactly the interference energy induced on the old task.
